title: A banked curve with no friction
caption: On a 15° bank the normal force tilts towards the centre. Its vertical part balances the weight and its horizontal part, mg tan 15°, is the centripetal force. Then v = √(gr tan θ) = 16.2 m s⁻¹ for r = 100 m.
alt: Free-body diagram of a car on a banked curve: weight down and a normal force tilted 15 degrees towards the centre, with the net force horizontal, towards the centre.
description: For a 1000 kg car: weight 9800 N down.
Normal force N = mg / cos 15° = 10146 N, tilted 15° from vertical towards the centre.
Net force: N sin 15° = mg tan 15° = 2626 N, horizontal, towards the centre.
mv²/r = mg tan θ, so v = √(9.8 × 100 × tan 15°) = 16.2 m s⁻¹.
